observations: Henry Ives Cobb; central rectangular hall and two polygonal pavilions joined by arcades.
Spanish-Romanesque appearance; fish/marine decoration on capitals, brackets and cornices; Spanish tile roof.
Text prints1100 ft extreme length. This is unresolved against the component dimensions and is NOT a calibrated compound envelope.
Main diagrams show a perimeter gallery around a long hall void and four straight stair locations beside entrance pavilions; two turret stair indications also appear.
Angling plan is16-sided, with radial installation partitions and a small central rotunda. Installation marks are not a structural bay schedule.
East aquarium text describes a60 ft rotunda,26 ft pool, rock mound with falling water, reeds and ten large tanks; the main hall includes boat/fisheries exhibits.

observations: Main building365 x165 ft; polygonal annexes133 ft6 in diameter; p75 alternatively says135 ft for aquarium.
Entrance pavilions102 ft long and projecting41 ft; paired round corner towers and upper bell stages.
Great circular upper story has a conical roof, open turret, four smaller towers and an exterior gallery.
Curved arcades, engaged column pairs and glazed Spanish tile roofs.
Aquarium rotunda60 ft; pool26 ft; ten larger tanks viewed from inner/outer paths; outer gallery about15 ft wide.

observations: Photograph of built work supports the great conical drum/lantern, four smaller towers, high clerestory hips, pointed entry gable, paired bell turrets, broad polygonal annex roofs and open arcades.
Monochrome perspective establishes visible forms, not numerical heights/pitches or exact colours. Rear elevation was not inspected.

limitations: Original main ground/gallery and angling installation diagrams, not complete as-built construction/elevation drawings. No aquarium construction diagram inspected.
Conkey1100 ft overall remains unresolved. Annex diameters133.5 and135 ft differ slightly; whole compound spacing is an authored choice.
Rear elevations, hidden joins, service rooms, structural engineering, exact roof pitches/heights and sculpture remain incomplete evidence.
Warm peach, ivory, soda-green glass and terracotta hues follow the user art direction; exact historical colours are unverified.
Aquarium tank footprints, rod displays, boats, railings and ornament are simplified interpretations, not exact historic exhibit placements.
Source wood/iron/steel/staff descriptions do not select collision, fuel or fire behaviour. Physical materials remain unassigned.
